title: Compatibility of a compactified graph map with a generator-preserving site comparison
statement: Let A,e,c,F,adj be as in the pro-etale compactification graph construction: A is a finite commutative ring, e:U -> T separated etale of finite type, c=(i:U -> Z,p:Z -> T) a compactification, and adj:F left adjoint to pro-etale restriction along e. Let C_X and R_X be the canonical site-comparison inverse and direct images [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Suppose sigma:e_!^et followed by C_T is isomorphic to C_U followed by F and its action on every raw lift generator is the pro-etale adjunction-unit generator of eta_U(m), after the comparison unit on T. Let G:F -> i_!^proet followed by p_*^proet have value the open-extension unit on the clopen graph specified by both projections, and zero on every complementary open, for every input sheaf and lift generator. Then for every etale sheaf M, sigma_M followed by G_(C_U M) equals C_T(G_M^et) followed by d_(i_!^et M) followed by p_*^proet(o_M). Here G^et is the existing canonical etaleCompactificationGraphMap [def-f7-etale-compactification-graph-map], o is the canonical open comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], and d is exactly mateEquiv of the inverse of the canonical comparisonCoefficientPullbackIso [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate, lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. No invertibility of d is assumed.

proof.text:
We compute the mate $d$ before using graphs. Direct-image evaluation [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] identifies $R_Tp_*^{\mathrm{proet}}=p_*^{\mathrm{et}}R_{\overline U}$: both evaluate a pro-etale sheaf on $\overline U\times_TW$ for etale $W$. The canonical $a^0:C_{\overline U}p_{\mathrm{et}}^*\cong p_{\mathrm{proet}}^*C_T$ is the left-adjoint comparison of this identity, as in [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. By the defining mate formula [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], the transpose of $d_{p,F}$ under $p_{\mathrm{proet}}^*\dashv p_*^{\mathrm{proet}}$ is $C_{\overline U}(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{et}}_{p,F})(a^0_{p_*^{\mathrm{et}}F})^{-1}$. By the normalization of $a^0$ as conjugate of the identity of right adjoints [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation, def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], for every $X$ one has $R_T(\eta^{\mathrm{proet}}_{p,C_TX})\eta_{T,X}=p_*^{\mathrm{et}}R_{\overline U}(a^0_X)\,p_*^{\mathrm{et}}(\eta_{\overline U,p_{\mathrm{et}}^*X})\,\eta^{\mathrm{et}}_{p,X}$. Expand $d_{p,F}=p_*^{\mathrm{proet}}(C_{\overline U}(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{et}}_{p,F})(a^0)^{-1})\eta^{\mathrm{proet}}_{p,C_Tp_*^{\mathrm{et}}F}$ and apply this with $X=p_*^{\mathrm{et}}F$: the factors $a^0$ and $(a^0)^{-1}$ cancel, so $R_T(d_{p,F})\eta_{T,p_*^{\mathrm{et}}F}=p_*^{\mathrm{et}}(R_{\overline U}C_{\overline U}(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{et}}_{p,F})\eta_{\overline U,p^*p_*F})\eta^{\mathrm{et}}_{p,p_*F}$. Naturality of $\eta_{\overline U}$ rewrites this as $p_*^{\mathrm{et}}(\eta_{\overline U,F})\,p_*^{\mathrm{et}}(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{et}}_{p,F})\eta^{\mathrm{et}}_{p,p_*F}$, and the $p$ triangle identity removes the last two factors. Hence
$$R_T(d_{p,F})\eta_{T,p_*^{\mathrm{et}}F}=p_*^{\mathrm{et}}(\eta_{\overline U,F}).$$
This computes the specified counit mate, with no invertibility assumption on $d$.

proof.text: The canonical etale graph map is defined by an etale base-change factor, a map q^* -> s_! for the clopen graph s, and the unit-preserving left-adjoint comparison s_! v_! = i_!. The base-change factor keeps the lift. The middle map is the graph inverse-image unit followed by the inverse of s_! -> s_*, so on a section it is the unique extension of m by zero off s. The last comparison preserves that value by its adjunction unit equation. Thus the formula in the existing definition has precisely the graph values m and zero used in Tag 0F4L.

proof.text: For $F=j_!^{\mathrm{et}}M$, set $h_M=R_{\overline U}(o_M)\eta_{\overline U,F}:F\to R_{\overline U}j_!^{\mathrm{proet}}C_UM$. The open unit normalization [lem-sf-open-comparison-unit-normalization], together with localized comparison [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism], says that the restriction of $h_M$ to $U$, under $j^*j_!M\cong M$ on both sites, is precisely $\eta_{U,M}$. Indeed [lem-pur-comparison-pullback-open-unit] identifies the restriction of $\eta_{\overline U,F}$ with the comparison unit on $F|_U$; then the open-unit equation for $o$ identifies that restricted map with $\eta_{U,M}$, using naturality in the open-unit isomorphism $M\cong j^*F$. The pro-etale open unit is an isomorphism by [lem-exc-proetale-open-unit]. Now take a raw generator $(W,t,m)$ and its etale graph extension $z=G_M^{\mathrm{et}}(t,m)$ on $H=\overline U\times_TW$. Restricting $h_M(z)$ to $\Gamma_t(W)$ gives $\eta_{U,M}(m)$ by the restriction equation, since the graph factors through $U$. Restricting to $D=H\setminus\Gamma_t(W)$ gives zero by naturality and additivity of $h_M$. The target is a sheaf, so its disjoint-open-cover axiom identifies $h_M(z)$ with the unique pro-etale graph extension of $\eta_{U,M}(m)$.

source.place: Tag 0F4L, lemma-shriek-into-star-separated-etale, clopen graph extension; proetale.tex Tag 09AF and the common-right-adjoint comparison

proof.text: Transpose both sides under C_T left adjoint to R_T. The assumed generator equation for sigma identifies the left transpose on (b,m) with the graph extension of eta_U(m). Naturality of the comparison unit and the mate identity in Step 1 identify the right transpose with the etale graph map followed by p_*(R_Z(o) eta_Z). Steps 2 and 3 give the same graph and complementary values, so disjoint-open sheaf separation identifies the sections. Transpose again under the etale sum adjunction: equality on every b and m is equality of the resulting sheaf maps. The two injective adjunction Hom bijections therefore identify the original maps. This is natural in the input sheaf.

theorem compactified_graph_comparison_of_generators
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    {U T : Scheme.{u}} (e : U ⟶ T) [Etale e] [IsSeparated e]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType e] [QuasiCompact e] (c : Compactification e)
    (F : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology U) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) ⥤
      Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology T) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A))
    (adj : F ⊣ localizationRestriction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) e inferInstance)
    (σ : Etale.etaleLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) e inferInstance ⋙
      comparisonUpperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) T ≅
        comparisonUpperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) U ⋙ F)
    (hσ : ∀ (M : Sheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) (b : U.Etale)
      (m : M.obj.obj (op b)),
      (((comparisonLowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) T).map
        (σ.hom.app M)).hom.app
          (op ((MorphismProperty.Over.map (P := @Etale) ⊤
            (inferInstance : Etale e)).obj b)))
        ((((comparisonAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) T).unit.app
          ((Etale.etaleLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) e inferInstance).obj M)).hom.app
            (op ((MorphismProperty.Over.map (P := @Etale) ⊤
              (inferInstance : Etale e)).obj b)))
          ((((Etale.etaleLowerShriekAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) e
            inferInstance).unit.app M).hom.app (op b)) m)) =
        ((adj.unit.app
          ((comparisonUpperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) U).obj M)).hom.app
            (op ((Scheme.toProEt U).obj b)))
          ((((comparisonAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) U).unit.app M).hom.app (op b)) m))
    (G : F ⟶
      openImmersionLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) c.i ⋙
        lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) c.g)
    (hG :
  ∀ (M : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology U) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) (b : U.ProEt),
    ∃ γ :
      (MorphismProperty.Over.map (P := @WeaklyEtale) ⊤
        (inferInstance : WeaklyEtale c.i)).obj b ⟶
      (MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @WeaklyEtale ⊤ c.g).obj
        ((MorphismProperty.Over.map (P := @WeaklyEtale) ⊤
          (inferInstance : WeaklyEtale e)).obj b),
      γ.left ≫ pullback.fst (b.hom ≫ e) c.g = 𝟙 b.left ∧
      γ.left ≫ pullback.snd (b.hom ≫ e) c.g = b.hom ≫ c.i ∧
      IsOpenImmersion γ.left ∧ IsClosedImmersion γ.left ∧
      ∀ m : M.obj.obj (op b),
        (((openImmersionLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) c.i).obj M).obj.map γ.op)
          (((G.app M).hom.app
            (op ((MorphismProperty.Over.map (P := @WeaklyEtale) ⊤
              (inferInstance : WeaklyEtale e)).obj b)))
            ((adj.unit.app M).hom.app (op b) m)) =
          (((openImmersionLowerShriekAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) c.i).unit.app M).hom.app
            (op b) m) ∧
        ∀ (D : c.Z.ProEt)
          (k : D ⟶ (MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @WeaklyEtale ⊤ c.g).obj
            ((MorphismProperty.Over.map (P := @WeaklyEtale) ⊤
              (inferInstance : WeaklyEtale e)).obj b)),
          IsOpenImmersion k.left → Set.range k.left = (Set.range γ.left)ᶜ →
          (((openImmersionLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) c.i).obj M).obj.map k.op)
            (((G.app M).hom.app
              (op ((MorphismProperty.Over.map (P := @WeaklyEtale) ⊤
                (inferInstance : WeaklyEtale e)).obj b)))
              ((adj.unit.app M).hom.app (op b) m)) = 0) :
    ∀ M : Sheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A),
        σ.hom.app M ≫
          G.app ((comparisonUpperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) U).obj M) =
        (comparisonUpperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) T).map
            ((Etale.etaleCompactificationGraphMap A e c).app M) ≫
          ((mateEquiv
            (Etale.upperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) c.g)
            (upperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) c.g)
            (TwoSquare.mk (comparisonUpperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) T)
              (Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) c.g)
              (upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) c.g)
              (comparisonUpperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) c.Z)
              (comparisonCoefficientPullbackIso (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) c.g).inv)).natTrans).app
            ((Etale.openImmersionLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) c.i).obj M) ≫
          (lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) c.g).map
            ((openImmersionLowerShriekComparisonUpperStarIso (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)
              c.i).hom.app M)
